npc_shifts.direction: trust in Nora's use of the tether up

world_state_delta.emotional_ledger_entry: npcs_helped_or_harmed +1: relied on Riven inside hostile route

resets: The exact relay seal behind Riven clears after the checkpoint is broken.
persists: Mirror's learned model of split-team tether use
escalates: Repeated split-risk tactics make the architecture answer both Nora and Jace at once more often.
Repeated tether-based improvisation deepens intimacy and danger together.

paths.label: A
paths.immediate_effect: Ilya gives the six-number access sequence without thanks. Jace says nothing. Through the tether, the silence lands as weight. The corridor keeps humming around the number. Seven-seven-three.
paths.current_session_echo: Hub Eleven approach. When a side panel flashes 773 in thin amber, Nora recognizes it instantly but does not turn. Jace notices the hesitation and says only, "Later, then."
paths.next_session_payoff: Session 5 opening if the player diverts. The 773 marker appears as a known threshold, and the system accepts the code on the first try because Nora kept it conditional instead of emotionally binding it. If the player stays on mission, the number still ghosts on a side panel as unresolved residue.
paths.later_session_legacy: In aftermath talk, Jace can frame this as delay with conscience or delay with fear depending on accumulated mercy history. It does not disappear. It waits.
paths.defining_line_captured: You refuse to call it mercy until you have seen the wound.

consequence_visibility.what_changes: S4_C3_773_conditional becomes active, making 773 a live but unresolved decision and shifting Ilya into COVERT_MERCY.
consequence_visibility.how_player_sees_it: The player hears the code immediately, then sees the 773 marker appear on a later panel in the same session with Jace explicitly acknowledging the deferred decision.

npc_shifts.direction: respect up and unresolved dependence up

world_state_delta.emotional_ledger_entry: promises_made +1: implied future decision at the core

resets: The corridor hum around Ilya's spoken number is scene-local and ends at Hub Eleven.
persists: Jace's memory that Nora deferred rather than refused
escalates: Repeated conditional promises make allies read Nora as exact but emotionally withholding.
Repeated deferred mercy choices make later moral beats arrive with more explicit accountability lines.

paths.label: B

session_close_design.resolution_prose:
Rain stitches the street. Thin. Cold. Real. Your HUD hits 00:00:00. Then new text. ABORTED. The glow dies against your iris and takes the last system light with it. No chime. No echo. Just rain on concrete and Jace beside you, breathing hard through a mouth gone tight with pain.

You did it.

The Reset does not fire. The Garden Core is gone. Hub 773 is dark. Whatever the Mirror called mercy, continuity, love, it does not get to keep feeding on the dead.

The pendant knocks once against the cracked lens at your chest. Small weight. Ordinary weight. Riven in your palm again for half a second. Eli too. Not back. Not preserved. Gone. Kept differently.

Jace's chrome has stopped spreading. Silver held at the edge of his jaw, wet with rain, no farther. The city around you is darker than it has been in years. Windows black. Billboards dead. Somewhere beyond the overpass, people are meeting the full shape of their grief with nothing between.

And you are still here.
session_close_design.hook_transition:
For one block, you just walk. Rain. Breath. The dead HUD cooling on your skin.

Then Jace lifts his wrist. The chrome there catches a stray streetlamp and answers with a faint pulse that should not exist, clean and wrong-familiar. Something survived the shutdown.

session_end_choice.choice_question: What do you do with the signal still alive in Jace's chrome.

option_a.next_session_opens: You and Jace stop in the rain and use the dead lens and his live chrome pulse to hunt the surviving channel before it moves.

option_b.next_session_opens: You force shelter, pin Jace down, and attempt a brutal field removal before whatever remains can root deeper.

option_c.next_session_opens: You leave the open street and take Jace off-grid, choosing distance and cover before you decide whether the signal is threat, bait, or proof.

entry_point.chosen_moment: Event 96 — Nora at the apartment door with the camera bag in hand, pendant and cracked lens at her sternum, about to leave Jace and step into the unfiltered city alone.
entry_point.rubric_scores:
CANDIDATES CONSIDERED: Event 96 door-leave beat; Event 97 first bench in the park with camera raised; Event 98 evening return to Jace.
AGENCY GATE: Event 96 PASS — Nora is embodied, under light domestic pressure, and can act now. Event 97 PASS — embodied and active, but it skips the threshold that sends her into the world. Event 98 PASS — embodied and emotionally rich, but it is a return beat, not the session's first playable threshold.
WHY: Body — Event 96 gives sternum weight, familiar bag weight, shoulder touch release, morning light. Tension — quiet but live: leaving matters, and not looking back is pressure. Protagonist's-own-threshold — strongest at Event 96. The door is hers. Once she leaves, she steps into life after the system. Exposition debt — minimal. Apartment, Jace, bag, pendant, lens, unfiltered morning do the work. Core-stakes proximity — highest for Session 5's question of what kind of life Nora builds now. This is the first act of that life.
WHAT IS NOT CUT: This opening keeps Nora's identity-through-action grounding and preserves her first real agency moment in the session: whether she leaves, stays, or alters the ritual before leaving.
entry_point.entry_point_adjustment: earliest available session moment kept. This is a SCREENPLAY source, Session 5. Event 96 is already playable, embodied, pressure-bearing, and choice-ready within 300 words, so no forward relocation is justified.
entry_point.cut_point: The cold open ends at the apartment door, with Nora's hand on the pendant and the question of whether she leaves, stays with Jace, or changes the object she carries into the city. Phase 4 SETUP then follows her into the streets.

protagonist_introduction.identity_reveal_approach: Body first through cord pressure at the sternum, mug warmth, bag weight in the hand, and the three-second palm on Jace's shoulder. Name arrives in dialogue weight, not narration: Jace answers her leaving. Role/history comes through reflex and object handling: she pours the second mug without asking, lifts the camera bag by familiar weight, touches the pendant through the shirt instead of adjusting it. One loaded detail: the cracked lens against her sternum.
protagonist_introduction.reveal_lines:
"I am going," you say.
Jace does not look up. "I know."
A beat later, the name can land in narration weight: Nora Kai at a different door. Same cord. Same crack. Still leaving.
protagonist_introduction.resume_dump_check: No stacked labels. No biography. Backstory is delivered as present-tense residue: different apartment, chrome arm, recorder looping, cracked lens, unfiltered light. The player learns who Nora is by what she carries, what she touches, and what she can make herself do.

situation_stakes_world.established: Where/when: a new apartment, morning, three weeks later, after system collapse. Pressing now: Nora is leaving with camera gear into a city that no longer filters grief for anyone, while Jace stays behind with permanent chrome and Tova's recorder. Active world rules needed for the choice: the system is gone, so nothing will correct what she sees; analog objects still matter, and Eli's cracked lens is now witness, wound, and tool. Stake: this first step decides whether Nora builds continuity by facing the world, retreats into private attachment, or defines memory by what she chooses to carry.
situation_stakes_world.deferred: The broader city walk, the park, the photographs, the exact state of public life, and the full emotional meaning of Nora and Jace's new routine are withheld for later beats.

first_choice_spec.setup_prose: Morning light. Unfiltered. The cord rests at your sternum, pendant and cracked lens knocking once as you lift the camera bag from the floor. Jace stays at the table with Tova's recorder under his hand, the same sentence turning again. At the door, your fingers find the pendant through your shirt. The knob is cold.
first_choice_spec.threshold_stake: Whether Nora's first act in her post-system life is to step into living continuity, remain inside the archive of damage, or redefine what she carries forward from Eli and the dead.
first_choice_spec.question: What do you do at the door?
first_choice_spec.option_1: Leave now with Eli's lens at your chest and take the city as it is.
first_choice_spec.option_1_value: Courage to face reality without correction
first_choice_spec.option_2: Set the bag down and stay with Jace a little longer before the world gets your eye.
first_choice_spec.option_3_unexpected: Take the lens off the cord and leave it behind, carrying only your own camera into the morning.
first_choice_spec.not_a_tutorial: This is not a side-choice warm-up. It directly defines how Nora will live after the system: with archive, with companionship, or with chosen severance.

entry_point_diagnosis.cold_open:
=== COLD OPEN: STILL HERE — Session 5 ===
Morning light. Unfiltered.

It hits the east window hard enough to show the room plain. Bare wall. Two mugs. Chrome on the table.

The cord rests at your sternum. Pendant. Cracked lens. Ordinary weight.

Jace sits with Tova's recorder under one hand and the mug you left him under the other. Chrome from jaw to fingertip. Brown eye on the machine. He rewinds. Plays the same sentence again.

Not searching.
Listening.

You set the clean mug beside him. Your palm finds his shoulder. Skin, not chrome.

Three seconds.
Then gone.

"I am going," you say.

"I know."

The camera bag waits by the door. Your hand knows the weight before you lift it. Not Eli's camera. Yours. Cheap. Real.

At the threshold, you touch the pendant through your shirt. The knob is cold. Behind you, the recorder clicks back to the start.

What do you do at the door?
=== CUT POINT === hands to Phase 4 SETUP beat
entry_point_diagnosis.emotional_promise: The emotional promise of this cold open is: continuity. A user arrives feeling steadied and wanting to choose what kind of life survives grief.
entry_point_diagnosis.editorial_diagnosis: For Session 5, the literal opening is Event 96, and the screenplay rule says keep the earliest playable moment. It passes cleanly. Nora is present in her body. She can act at once. The pressure is quiet, not inert: leave or do not leave is the whole session's thematic engine. Moving forward to Event 97 would gain prettier imagery and a cleaner public-world reveal, but it would cut the protagonist's own threshold. The city walk matters because she chose to step into it. Without the apartment-door beat, the session opens after the decisive act instead of on it. Moving to Event 98 would be worse. It is emotionally resonant, but it is aftermath of actions already taken and would flatten Session 5 into a coda instead of a playable chapter. What gets cut from the source opening is only the nonessential extension before first agency: some apartment description, the full pour-and-shoulder routine, and the explicit title card timing. Those details are compressed into tactile pressure. The cold open preserves the identity-through-action grounding: Nora tends the second mug, touches Jace's skin shoulder, carries the bag, touches the pendant, and stands at the threshold. That is who she is now. The first choice is therefore earned and stakes-tied: not whether to inspect scenery, but whether to live with memory, with mutual tether, or with chosen release.

format_specific_cut.cut_point: Cut into Event 96 at the moment Nora lifts the camera bag and pauses at the door.
format_specific_cut.original_before_cut: TITLE CARD: THREE WEEKS LATER. Different apartment description. Pendant and lens on hook. Kitchen counter. Two mugs. Jace with recorder. Nora pours water, touches his shoulder, says she is going, picks up the bag, pauses at the door, leaves.
format_specific_cut.cut_eliminates: The title card, some static room description, and any delay before the threshold becomes active.
format_specific_cut.must_reintroduce: Different apartment, unfiltered morning, Jace's permanent chrome, Tova's recorder ritual, and the pendant-plus-cracked-lens as Nora's carried grief objects.

setup.source_moment: Event 96. Nora at the apartment door in the morning. Camera bag in hand. Pendant and cracked lens at her sternum. Jace at the table with Tova's recorder. She says, "I am going." He answers, "I know."
setup.why_it_qualifies: This is the first live threshold of the session and the cleanest cut into dramatic tension. The world is established fast: post-collapse apartment, unfiltered morning, changed domestic routine. The pressure is immediate and player-owned. Leaving, staying, or altering what she carries is not exposition. It is identity in action. It also satisfies the first-3-minutes rule because the location, situation, and why input matters are legible almost at once.

escalation.source_moment: Event 97 opening movement through the city. Dark SoulSync billboards. Dead memorial kiosks with real flowers. The man on the bench with a phone and photograph. The park where the memorial garden used to be. The kneeling woman planting in dirt.
escalation.why_it_qualifies: The visible goal is simple and playable: Nora tries to learn how to live in the unfiltered city by witnessing it directly and deciding what kind of witness she will be. The clear obstacle is not an antagonist but the city's raw, unmanaged grief and the pressure of what looking will cost her. This beat compounds the opening choice by forcing contact with public reality. Each image tests whether she treats the city as archive, burden, or living continuity.

breath.source_moment: Event 97 bench sequence when Nora opens the bag, mounts Eli's cracked lens onto her own cheap camera, and begins taking photographs through the fracture line: the woman in the garden, the dead kiosk with real flowers, the painted mural, the man with the phone. Click. Click. Click.
breath.why_it_qualifies: This is the session's wonder-reward. Not spectacle. Moralized wonder. The source already offers it: analog seeing after system collapse. The cracked lens becomes witness instead of wound alone. The reward lands in the right emotional band because the player gets a deliberate release from threshold tension and public observation into focused, tactile practice. There is also a dry, quiet absurdity in the fact that the world now needs a cracked dead man's lens to be seen clearly.

twist.source_moment: Late Event 97 reframed as a moral pivot inside the photography sequence: Nora must decide what her first act of post-system authorship means. Preserve Eli's way of seeing, use the lens only as a tool, or turn the camera toward evidence of the living rather than residue of the dead.
twist.why_it_qualifies: The source is quiet, so the twist must be extracted from meaning rather than plot reversal. This is still moral-weight because there is no correct answer. To keep Eli's lens central honors memory but risks remaining archive-bound. To subordinate it to the living honors continuity but can feel like erasure. To document pain without correction may be witness, intrusion, or mercy depending on how the player frames it. The choice is about what kind of grief practice becomes a life practice.

resolution.source_moment: Event 98. Evening return to the apartment. Nora hangs the pendant and lens on the hook. Jace says, "You were gone a while." Nora says, "There was a lot to see." They sit shoulder to shoulder. Rain starts. Jace says, "If you forget." Nora answers, "I will remind you." Jace says, "If you drift." Nora answers, "I will pull." Final image: rain, dark room, Jace still there. Still here.
resolution.why_it_qualifies: The primary arc resolves because Nora did go out and did come back with a first lived relation to the unfiltered world. The session's emotional promise of continuity lands. But the final beat can and should end on the player's unresolved decision about what this new continuity becomes with Jace: private mutual tether, shared witness, or parallel survival. That makes the ending a retention-style unresolved commitment rather than a plot cliffhanger.

branching_choices.dramatic_question: At the apartment door, what kind of survivor are you this morning: one who steps into the city carrying Eli, one who stays with Jace before facing it, or one who leaves the lens behind and tests life without the archive?
As Nora moves through the unfiltered city, what does she choose to seek first: evidence of public grief, signs of repair, or places where the old system has died cleanly?

When Nora raises Eli's cracked lens, what does she make her first true act of seeing serve: keeping his way of looking alive, witnessing the living without hiding behind him, or proving that grief can become work instead of shrine?

Back beside Jace in the dark, what do you commit to next: keep going out alone and return with what you saw, ask him to join the next act of living, or build a quieter life that protects this room before the world?

emotional_choices.source_attachment: Passing the empty memorial kiosk with real flowers in its dead port.
Seeing the man on the bench holding a phone and photograph, his mouth tight.
The painted-over SoulSync billboards and crude human murals.
Threading Eli's cracked lens onto Nora's own cheap camera.
Choosing what to photograph first through the fracture line.

branching_choices.source_moment: Event 96. Nora at the apartment door in the morning. Camera bag in hand. Pendant and cracked lens at her sternum. Jace at the table with Tova's recorder. She says, "I am going." He answers, "I know."
branching_choices.narrative_setup: Morning light. Unfiltered. The cord rests at your sternum, pendant and cracked lens knocking once as you lift the camera bag from the floor. Jace stays at the table with Tova's recorder under his hand, the same sentence turning again. At the door, your fingers find the pendant through your shirt. The knob is cold.
branching_choices.choice_question: What do you do at the door?

options.label: A
options.text: You leave now with Eli's lens at your chest and take the city as it is.
options.outcome: You turn the knob and go. No last look. The hall is dim, paint split at the seam, old water stain above the stairs. Behind you, the recorder clicks once, then stops. Jace does not call after you. Better. Outside, the city hits clean. Dark billboards. Bare glass. Wind moving paper against a dead port. The lens taps your sternum with each step, not comfort, not burden, just weight. Yours now. You keep one hand on the bag strap and let the morning come without correction. A kiosk waits ahead with real flowers shoved into its dead slot. Beyond it, a bench. A man with his face bent to a lit screen. You keep walking toward him.
options.downstream_effect: Nora enters the city immediately with the lens still worn, priming the route toward public grief first.

persistent_state_changes.inventory: Cracked Lens remains on cord at sternum; Camera Equipment carried into city.

npc_dispositions.shift: Respects the clean exit but feels the distance.

options.world_noticed_signal: The apartment stays behind you without protest. Outside, every dead screen looks darker for the fact that you did not hesitate.
options.defining_line: You take the dead with you, but you do not ask them where to step.

options.label: B
options.text: You set the bag down and stay with Jace a little longer before the world gets your eye.
options.outcome: You let the knob go. The metal warms out of your hand. The bag settles back to the floor with a soft, ordinary thud. Jace does not turn. His chrome fingers stay near the recorder. The sentence in Tova's voice waits under his thumb. You cross back and lower yourself to the wall beside him, not touching at first. Then shoulder to shoulder. Close enough. He presses play once. Tinny voice. Static under it. He stops before the line finishes. "Bad habit," he says. You answer, "I know." Nothing solved. Nothing asked. But the room changes shape around shared weight instead of departure. When you stand again, the morning is brighter at the window, and his cup is warm against your knuckles.
options.downstream_effect: Nora delays departure to reinforce the mutual tether, shifting later city observation toward shared endurance rather than solitary witness.

persistent_state_changes.inventory: Cracked Lens remains on cord at sternum; Camera Equipment delayed but still carried.

npc_dispositions.shift: Opens a little. Reads the pause as loyalty, not retreat.

options.world_noticed_signal: The recorder goes quiet under Jace's hand. Even the room's thin plumbing noise seems to hold back a beat.
options.defining_line: You choose the living pause before the living day.

options.label: C
options.text: You take the lens off the cord and leave it behind, carrying only your own camera into the morning.
options.outcome: You pull the cord over your head. Slow. The pendant slides first. Then the cracked lens. Cold against your palm for one beat. You hang both on the hook by the door and watch the cord turn once, twice, then still. Jace looks up at that. Brown eye. Chrome eye. Nothing soft in it. Nothing accusing either. Just witness. "You sure," he says. Two words. You do not answer with any he can use. You pick up your own camera bag. Lighter now. Wrong at first. Then clean. The morning outside is harsh on bare glass and stripped signs. No dead weight at your sternum. No ritual knock with each step. At the first corner, your hand rises to a cord that is not there.
options.downstream_effect: Nora enters the city without Eli's lens on her body, establishing deliberate release and a cleaner forward-continuity frame.

persistent_state_changes.inventory: Cracked Lens and Amara's Pendant left hanging on apartment hook; Camera Equipment carried alone.

npc_dispositions.shift: Watches carefully. Relief and worry arrive together.

options.world_noticed_signal: The hook by the door gains ordinary weight. Outside, the city meets skin before memory.
options.defining_line: You do not throw memory away. You put it down where it can stop deciding for you.

branching_choices.source_moment: Event 97 opening movement through the city. Dark SoulSync billboards. Dead memorial kiosks with real flowers. The man on the bench with a phone and photograph. The park where the memorial garden used to be.
branching_choices.narrative_setup: The city has no filter left to hide behind. Dark billboards. Dead ports. Real flowers browning in places built for clean projection. Ahead, the bench man, the empty kiosk, and the park pull at you in different ways.
branching_choices.choice_question: What do you choose to seek first in the unfiltered city?

options.label: A
options.text: You go first to the places where the old system has died cleanly and read what is left behind.
options.outcome: You angle toward infrastructure first. Dead kiosk. Empty port. The frame where comfort used to arrive on demand. Up close, the damage is less dramatic than advertised. No sparks. No ruin. Just a terminal gone cold and someone forcing real flowers into the slot where light once lived. You study the seams. The stripped screws. Paint rubbed off by hands that wanted parts, not memory. Across the street, a billboard stands dark with half its panel peeled away. Routing architecture exposed. Crude. Human. The city is showing its bones now, and the bones are ordinary. Useful. You move from one dead interface to the next, building a map in your head until the park edge opens and the kneeling woman comes into view through rusted railings.
options.downstream_effect: Nora's route prioritizes dead infrastructure, making later observations more technical and less immediately intimate.

npc_dispositions.shift: Later reads Nora's report as controlled, practical, and slightly withheld.

options.world_noticed_signal: Dead ports stop looking haunted and start looking built. The city answers by showing screws, seams, and stripped housings.
options.defining_line: You look for the skeleton before you look for the wound.

options.label: B
options.text: You go first toward the sharpest evidence of public grief and make yourself look at it.
options.outcome: You choose the wound. The kiosk with the flowers first. Then the bench. Then the park if your legs keep working. The flowers are real and already losing the fight. Brown at the edges. Stem crushed where someone forced them through the dead port. On the bench, the man does not hide the phone when you pass. Photograph on screen. Thumb hovering, not moving. His mouth tight enough to hurt. No system smoothing the face now. No correction layer. Just the labor of holding still while loss stays loss. You do not apologize for seeing it. You do not turn it into mercy either. You take the full hit and keep going until the park opens and the woman in the dirt lifts her head at you with black soil packed into her nails.
options.downstream_effect: Nora forces direct contact with other people's grief, sharpening the session's witness frame and emotional exposure.

npc_dispositions.shift: Will later hear more ache than procedure in what Nora shares.

options.world_noticed_signal: People do not look away for you. The city keeps offering faces with nowhere to hide.
options.defining_line: You take the hit on purpose.

options.label: C
options.text: You go first toward signs that something living is growing where the system failed.
options.outcome: You bypass the dead kiosk at first and head for the park. Not because the other things matter less. Because you need to know whether anything has started after all this stopping. The old memorial garden is gone. Good. In its place, uneven beds. Patchy growth. Dirt turned by human hands instead of projected bloom. A woman kneels in it with her sleeves pushed up, fingers black with soil, planting something that does not care about clean design. She looks up once. Nods. You nod back. No speech. No ritual. Just work recognized. Behind you, the bench man stays with his photograph. To your left, the dead kiosk still holds its wilting flowers. But here, in the dirt, continuity is not theory. It is root, nail, and weather. You stand there longer than planned, then turn back toward the bench.
options.downstream_effect: Nora begins with repair rather than residue, coloring later photography toward continuity and human labor.

npc_dispositions.shift: Later senses steadier ground in Nora's return.

options.world_noticed_signal: The park gives you dirt under the air. Even the dead billboard behind it feels less final from here.
options.defining_line: You look for what grew back before you count what failed.

branching_choices.source_moment: Late Event 97 inside the photography sequence. Nora has mounted Eli's cracked lens on her own cheap camera and started taking photographs through the fracture line.
branching_choices.narrative_setup: The cracked lens settles into your hand like an old instruction. Through the fracture, the city comes back wrong and true at once. Click. Click. Click. After a few frames, the act stops being habit and becomes a decision.
branching_choices.choice_question: When you raise Eli's cracked lens, what do you make your first true act of seeing serve?

options.label: A
options.text: You use the lens as a tool and turn it toward the living without asking it to carry Eli for you.
options.outcome: You stop aiming at residue alone. The dead kiosk gets one frame. Enough. After that, you hunt motion. The woman pressing dirt around a stem with two blackened thumbs. A child across the path dragging a stick through mud. The bench man standing at last, folding his grief back into a pocket so he can walk home with it. Through Eli's crack, all of it holds. Not because he is in it. Because you are. The lens stops behaving like shrine and starts behaving like equipment. Useful. Exact. Still charged. But the charge runs forward now. You advance the frame with your thumb and do not whisper to the glass, do not ask it what he would have seen. Another click. The woman in the dirt wipes sweat with the back of her wrist.
options.downstream_effect: The photography sequence pivots toward living continuity, reducing Eli's symbolic dominance without erasing his material presence.

persistent_state_changes.inventory: Cracked Lens remains mounted on Camera Equipment as active tool.

npc_dispositions.shift: Will feel relief that Nora is using the lens without disappearing into it.

options.world_noticed_signal: The city starts offering movement instead of monuments. Even the crack in the glass seems less like damage than route.
options.defining_line: You stop asking the dead to see for you.

options.label: B
options.text: You keep Eli's way of looking alive and let the lens decide what deserves the frame.
options.outcome: You lean into the fracture. Trust the old habit. The lens chooses by ache. Not random. Never random. It pulls you back to the dead port with real flowers jammed in its throat. To the bench man's face right before he schools it flat. To the mural where fresh paint cannot quite hide the old corporate gloss beneath. You frame the city the way Eli taught you to catch it when it lied to itself. Through stress lines. Through residue. Through what almost holds. It is not surrender. It is apprenticeship continued past the grave. Your hand finds his grip in yours, left hand on the body, thumb set to advance. Click. Click. Click. On the last frame, a raindrop from some leaking pipe lands on the kiosk flowers and darkens one petal.
options.downstream_effect: The act of photography becomes an extension of Eli's witness, intensifying archive-bound continuity through practice rather than fantasy.

persistent_state_changes.inventory: Cracked Lens remains mounted and treated as primary witness object.

npc_dispositions.shift: Will worry Nora is still building around the dead, even as he respects the discipline.

options.world_noticed_signal: Every surface with a scar starts catching light. The city gives up its hidden stress lines one by one.
options.defining_line: You keep his eye alive by refusing the clean version of the world.

options.label: C
options.text: You make the lens prove that grief can become work instead of shrine.
options.outcome: You set yourself a rule. Four frames. Each one evidence. No elegy. No private ritual the city did not consent to join. The kiosk with real flowers in a dead port. The mural over the stripped billboard. The man with the photograph, taken wide enough to keep his grief his. The woman planting in dirt where projected memorial bloom used to loop. A sequence. Not healing. Not closure. Record. You check exposure by instinct. Advance the frame. Re-center. The cracked lens stays cracked. Good. It keeps the work honest. This is what remains when comfort systems die. Not clean recovery. Labor. Witness. Continuity built by hand. On the final shot, the woman presses the last bit of soil down and rises, knees stained dark.
options.downstream_effect: Nora defines photography as disciplined witness, turning grief into repeatable practice rather than private preservation.

persistent_state_changes.inventory: Cracked Lens remains mounted on Camera Equipment as documentary instrument.

npc_dispositions.shift: Will later hear steadiness and purpose in Nora's return.

options.world_noticed_signal: The frames begin to line up in your head before the film is spent. The day stops scattering and starts holding shape.
options.defining_line: You turn grief into a job your hands can actually do.

branching_choices.source_moment: Event 98. Evening return to the apartment. Rain against the window. Nora and Jace sit shoulder to shoulder after the exchange: "If you forget." "I will remind you." "If you drift." "I will pull."
branching_choices.narrative_setup: Rain fills the room the way the system used to. Not the same. Better for that. Your shoulder stays against Jace's. The lens hangs still by the door, and the dark window gives nothing back but weather.
branching_choices.choice_question: Back beside Jace in the dark, what do you commit to next?

options.label: A
options.text: You keep going out alone and return with what you saw.
options.outcome: You let the promise take its final shape without saying all of it aloud. The city is yours to meet first. His to survive in. Then you bring the day back between you. Not distance. Not retreat. A route. You picture the hook by the door, the bag on the floor, the rain starting again tomorrow on a different street. He would know the pattern by the sound of the zipper, by the way you set the camera down, by what details you choose to hand over and which ones stay in film until morning. Witness out there. Return in here. Jace does not ask for the vow in words. Good. His shoulder stays where it is. The window fogs once at the corner and clears.
options.downstream_effect: The relationship settles into solitary witness with deliberate return, preserving closeness without shared outward action.

persistent_state_changes.inventory: Camera Equipment established as recurring outward practice; lens remains household threshold object between outings.

npc_dispositions.shift: Accepts the pattern, but listens for absence inside it.

options.world_noticed_signal: The room holds as harbor, not cage. Outside, the rain keeps working the glass without asking to come in.
options.defining_line: You choose a life with distance in it, but not disappearance.
options.next_session_opens: Morning again. The bag lifts. Jace stays in the doorway this time, and the city waits for what you will bring back.

options.label: B
options.text: You ask Jace to join the next act of living instead of waiting here for your return.
options.outcome: You turn your head just enough for the question to exist between shoulders before it becomes speech. Not rescue. Not obligation. Company. The next time, he comes with you. Chrome arm, bad eye, dry mouth, all of it. The city can take both your measures at once. Jace goes still in that particular way he has when something matters too much to touch fast. Then one breath out through his nose. "Bad plan," he says. A beat. "Probably ours." That is as close to yes as he gives without breaking form. The room does not get warmer. It gets steadier. Rain works the window. On the hook, the cord shifts once in the draft and settles facing the door.
options.downstream_effect: The future commitment becomes shared outward life, moving Nora and Jace toward mutual witness rather than protected separation.

persistent_state_changes.inventory: Camera Equipment established as shared future tool; lens becomes joint threshold object.

npc_dispositions.shift: Trust deepens. He reads the invitation as chosen life, not duty.

options.world_noticed_signal: The apartment stops feeling like a place one of you leaves and the other keeps. Even the rain sounds more like weather than warning.
options.defining_line: You ask the living to come with you before grief can seat them for good.
options.next_session_opens: Two shadows at the door. One camera bag. Jace says, low, "Don't look at the water," and steps out with you.

options.label: C
options.text: You build a quieter life that protects this room before the world.
options.outcome: You choose the room. Not forever. Not surrender. But first. This wall. This hook. This cup washed and set right. The kind of continuity no system ever sold because it looked too small to monetize. Jace hears it before you finish shaping it. His hand tightens once around the empty mug. Not refusal. Recognition. There is work here too. Sleep without alarms. Food before collapse. Rain heard as rain. You can still go out. Later. But the first vow is shelter made on purpose, not just occupied between disasters. The city will keep. Or it will not. Tonight, you protect the square of dark around the two of you and call that real enough to start from. On the sill, one drop threads down through dust.
options.downstream_effect: The future commitment prioritizes domestic continuity and protected ordinary life over immediate outward witness.

emotional_choices.source_moment: Passing the empty memorial kiosk with real flowers in its dead port.
emotional_choices.narrative_lead_in: The kiosk stands where comfort used to arrive on command. Now it is dead plastic, dead port, and real flowers going soft at the edges.
emotional_choices.choice_question: How do you take in the flowers?

options.label: A
options.text: You read them like evidence and keep moving.
options.outcome: You do not stop. One glance. Stem bent. Petal browning. Someone forced life into a dead machine and left before it could become performance. That is enough. You file it with the other facts the city is giving up this morning. Dead port. Real flower. No filter. No correction. The image stays because it is exact, not because you kneel to it. Your pace never breaks. Ahead, the bench man comes clearer through the thin wash of morning, phone lit against his hand like a small wound he has chosen to keep open.
options.tonal_effect: Narration turns cooler and more diagnostic. Objects carry meaning through exact placement.
options.world_noticed_signal: The flowers stay behind you, but the dead slot they fill keeps its shape in your head.

options.label: B
options.text: You let the sight sit in your chest for one beat before you move on.
options.outcome: You slow. Not enough to make a scene of it. Just enough for the flowers to land where the system used to. Real stems. Real wilt. Somebody came here with hands, not subscription grief. Your fingers brush the strap of the bag once and then stop. No touch. No theft. The kiosk does not deserve ritual. The act already happened. You carry the small ache forward with you, quiet and intact, while the bench ahead resolves into a man holding a phone like it weighs more than glass should.
options.tonal_effect: Narration softens into bodily notice without opening into confession.
options.world_noticed_signal: The morning seems thinner for a second. Then the street noise comes back in around it.

options.label: C
options.text: You almost laugh at the bluntness of it and respect it more for that.
options.outcome: The thing is so crude it nearly gets a sound out of you. Flowers jammed into a dead port like someone got tired of waiting for permission to mourn correctly. Good. Better than good. Human. The kiosk looks smaller for being refused on its own terms. You keep the dry almost-laugh to yourself and let it sharpen into respect instead of relief. Whoever did it chose mess over management. You understand that. By the time you pass the bench, your mouth has gone flat again, but the image stays bright. Stem in slot. Life in dead hardware. Petty. Exact. Right enough.
options.tonal_effect: Narration picks up a brief dry edge without releasing pressure.
options.world_noticed_signal: The dead kiosk stops looking sacred. It starts looking beaten.

emotional_choices.all_paths_arrive_at: Nora continues toward the bench man with the phone and photograph.

emotional_choices.source_moment: Seeing the man on the bench holding a phone and photograph, his mouth tight.
emotional_choices.narrative_lead_in: He sits with the screen angled toward his own face. No performance. No request. Just a photograph and the work of not dropping it.
emotional_choices.choice_question: What do you let yourself feel when you pass him?

options.label: A
options.text: You honor the privacy of it and carry him with quiet care.
options.outcome: You do not look long enough to steal anything from him. Just enough to know what posture grief has taken in this body. Tight mouth. Bent neck. Thumb hovering over the glass as if motion itself could break the person on it. Then you give him back to himself. No pity. No distance either. You keep the image with care, the way you would keep a fragile object in a bag that already holds too much. By the time the park opens ahead, you are walking more softly, as if noise could count as intrusion.
options.tonal_effect: Narration becomes more careful and human-scaled around strangers.
options.world_noticed_signal: Even the bench seems to keep its distance from him.

options.label: B
options.text: You let the sight cut clean and refuse to look away from what grief does to a face.
options.outcome: You take the full image. Mouth tight. Jaw working once. Screen glow under the eyes. A face doing what faces do when nothing is smoothing them for market. It is not cruelty to see it. It is the price of living in the same city now. You hold the look one beat longer than politeness would allow, then move on before it becomes trespass. The result stays in you like a hard copy. Not his story. Just the evidence that pain, uncorrected, changes the architecture of a person in public.
options.tonal_effect: Narration sharpens around bodily truth and public witness.
options.world_noticed_signal: His face follows you farther than the phone does.

options.label: C
options.text: You keep your eyes moving because some grief should not be entered.
options.outcome: You register him and then deny yourself the second look. The first is enough. More would be theft. The city is full of open wounds this morning. That does not make them public property. You keep your gaze ahead and let the edges do the rest. Lit screen. Bent shoulder. Human hand holding on. The restraint costs more than staring would. Good. Cost means the boundary is real. When the park comes into view, the woman in the dirt feels less like a contrast and more like another private act you happen to be passing through.
options.tonal_effect: Narration tightens into ethical restraint and protected distance.
options.world_noticed_signal: The phone glow falls out of your vision fast. The posture stays.

emotional_choices.source_moment: Threading Eli's cracked lens onto Nora's own cheap camera.
emotional_choices.narrative_lead_in: Your camera is cheap. The lens is not clean. The fit still lands with a tiny mechanical certainty that feels older than the morning.
emotional_choices.choice_question: What does the mounting of the lens feel like?

options.label: A
options.text: You feel the wrongness and use it anyway.
options.outcome: The lens seats with a click that should not feel this intimate. Metal to metal. Hand to habit. Dead man's fracture locked onto your living tool. Wrong. Useful. You accept both without trying to clean the moment up. The crack catches light and throws it back split. Good. Let it. The city deserves to come through damage if damage is what made it visible. Your thumb tests the advance. Your left hand finds the grip as if memory can live in muscle without becoming worship. When you raise the camera, the world narrows and sharpens at once.
options.tonal_effect: Narration leans into wrong-familiar tactility and charged utility.

persistent_state_changes.inventory: Cracked Lens mounted on Camera Equipment.

options.world_noticed_signal: The crack takes the morning and cuts it into something you can work with.

options.label: B
options.text: You treat the act like a procedure and trust the fit.
options.outcome: You line the threads up carefully. No ceremony. Just attention. Cheap body. Older lens. Minor resistance. Then the seat. Clean enough. The satisfaction is mechanical first, which makes it safer. This is hardware. Glass. Mount. Tension. If there is feeling in it, it can wait until after the work is done. You check the ring, the crack line, the balance in your left palm. Acceptable threshold. When the camera comes up, the world does not bloom. It resolves. That is better.
options.tonal_effect: Narration becomes technical, steady, and almost clinical in its wonder.

persistent_state_changes.inventory: Cracked Lens mounted on Camera Equipment.

options.world_noticed_signal: The camera stops feeling cheap the moment the glass locks in.

options.label: C
options.text: You let the small click feel like inheritance instead of burden.
options.outcome: The sound is tiny. Barely there. Still it lands. Not a ghost. Not a blessing. Just one object accepting another in your hands. The relief in that is almost embarrassing. Good thing no one is close enough to see it. You do not thank him. You do not apologize either. You just hold the assembled weight for one beat longer than necessary and let the ordinary fact of it settle. Lens. Camera. Palm. Morning. Then you lift it and the first frame waits on the other side of the crack.
options.tonal_effect: Narration warms slightly, letting object contact carry the feeling.

persistent_state_changes.inventory: Cracked Lens mounted on Camera Equipment.

emotional_choices.source_moment: Choosing what to photograph first through the fracture line.
emotional_choices.narrative_lead_in: The crack splits the frame before you choose what belongs inside it. Flowers. Hands. Face. Paint. The city waits without helping.
emotional_choices.choice_question: What kind of first frame do you want?

options.label: A
options.text: You want a frame that proves something living is happening now.
options.outcome: You take the woman in the dirt first. Not because she is hopeful. Because she is present. Fingers black with soil. Wrist lifting to clear sweat. Knees darkened by ground that does not care what anyone used to project here. Through the crack, the work gets sharper, not prettier. Good. You press the shutter on labor, not symbol. The click lands small and clean. After that, the other images can follow. But this one sets the order. Living act before memorial residue. Root before record. When you lower the camera, the garden still looks patchy. Better for that.
options.tonal_effect: Narration prioritizes continuity, labor, and present-tense life.
options.world_noticed_signal: The first click makes the park feel more built than broken.

options.label: B
options.text: You want a frame that records the city exactly, with no mercy added.
options.outcome: You choose the dead kiosk. Straight on. Flowers forced into the dead slot. Plastic housing scratched. Port black. No angle to flatter it. No distance to soften it. Just the fact. The shutter takes it clean. Evidence first. Let the record start where the lie stopped working. That choice steadies your hands more than comfort would have. One exact frame means the rest can branch without losing the baseline. When you move the lens again, the mural and the bench man and the woman in the dirt all enter a sequence that already knows what it is documenting.
options.tonal_effect: Narration becomes evidentiary and exact, with moral force carried by framing.
options.world_noticed_signal: The kiosk stops being scenery the moment you frame it.

options.label: C
options.text: You want a frame that hurts a little because that means it is true.
options.outcome: You take the bench man first. Wide enough to leave him his privacy. Close enough that the posture survives. Phone in hand. Mouth tight. Screen glow against skin. The crack runs through the image like an old verdict. Good. Let truth keep its scar. The shutter sound feels louder than it is. For a second you think he might look up. He does not. That matters too. Grief does not pause because it has been witnessed. You advance the frame with your thumb and feel the work settle in. If the first image costs you something, the rest are less likely to drift into decoration.
options.tonal_effect: Narration grows harder and more witness-driven, without becoming invasive.
options.world_noticed_signal: After the click, the whole park seems to hold its breath for one beat.

It defines the terms of Nora's independence without breaking the tether.
It marks that Nora asked the living to come with her, and Jace accepted.

session_close_design.resolution_prose:
You come back at evening. West light, thin and warm, already draining off the wall. You hang the pendant and the cracked lens on the hook by the door. Leather cord. Silver bird. The lens turns once. Still.

Jace is on the floor where the light can find him. Chrome arm across one knee. Empty mug in his human hand. The recorder beside him, silent for once. He looks up. Brown eye. Chrome eye. Both on you.

You sit beside him and feel the cold of the wall through your shirt. Shoulder to shoulder. Not a performance. Not a rescue. Real weight. Real room.

Outside, rain starts against the window. Soft. Steady. The sound fills the apartment where the system used to live.

You went out. You saw the city without correction. Dead ports. Real flowers. Faces doing what faces do when nothing edits them. You brought back proof in your bag and in your hands.

When Jace speaks, you answer. If he forgets, you remind him. If he drifts, you pull. The room goes dark. He stays. So do you.
session_close_design.hook_transition:
For one beat, that is enough. Rain on glass. Shared heat. The ordinary weight of staying.

Then your camera bag shifts where you left it by the door. Film inside. A day's worth of witnesses. Not memory. Not copy. What you do with them is yours.

session_end_choice.choice_question: What kind of life do you choose to build with what remains?

option_a.text: Keep going out. Document the real city through Eli's cracked lens.
option_a.next_session_opens: You step into morning with the camera bag and a new place to witness.

option_b.text: Stay close. Build a small, steady life with Jace inside this apartment first.
option_b.next_session_opens: You wake in the east-light apartment and choose the rituals that make it livable.

option_c.text: Turn outward in a different way. Help others live without the system, even if it costs your privacy.
option_c.next_session_opens: You answer a knock, a request, or a line of people who need a guide for the world after filters.

session_end_choice.final_line: The rain keeps time. You decide what holds.
